title: Report on Studying in Adelaide
paragraphs: I enrolled in the Nagoya University-University of Adelaide Joint Degree Program in Medical Sciences in October 2015, and I was allowed to study at the University of Adelaide in Australia for three and a half years, from October 2017 to March 2021. I spent my research life in the Gastrointestinal Cancer Laboratory (laboratory heads: Dr. Daniel Worthley and Associate Professor Susan Woods) at SAHMRI (South Australian Health and Medical Research Institute; the building in the photo). At both Nagoya University and the University of Adelaide, I was able to carry out consistent research on the microenvironment of colorectal cancer, in particular on "cancer-associated fibroblasts." We found that two fibroblast markers, each of which had been the focus of the host laboratory abroad and of the Department of Tumor Pathology at Nagoya University respectively, are expressed in different cell subpopulations and respectively promote and suppress colorectal cancer progression, and we were able to put this together into one paper proposing the heterogeneity of cancer-associated fibroblasts (Kobayashi et al., Gastroenterology, 2021). We also clarified part of the origin of cancer-associated fibroblasts in colorectal cancer through a joint study between the University of Adelaide and Nagoya University (Kobayashi et al., Gastroenterology, 2022). In the Joint Degree Program (JDP), I feel that I acquired the ability to carry out research by working in an excellent research environment and receiving guidance from supervisors at both Nagoya University and the University of Adelaide. I came to realise that it is important for this that the research fields of the two laboratories match (or that the themes are set so that they overlap) and that the supervisors of both universities are cooperative with the JDP. Because I was the first student in the JDP, I also experienced many difficulties. It is hard to carry out the experiments of a single consistent project in Japan and abroad (especially mouse experiments), and I received a great deal of cooperation from the doctors of the Department of Tumor Pathology at Nagoya University. In addition, in Australia, where the idea of animal welfare is widespread, animal ethics are very strict, so ethics applications for animal experiments have to be prepared carefully. Also, the way of thinking about degrees differs between Nagoya and Adelaide, and it took time to make myself understood. In the doctoral course of the Nagoya University Graduate School of Medicine and in the JDP, writing a first-author paper is essential for obtaining the degree, but in Adelaide it is not required. Perhaps for this reason, the work of several graduate students and postdocs is sometimes combined into one large paper. In this case, unless one's contribution to the paper is the highest, one cannot publish the paper as first author and obtain the JDP degree, so I think it is necessary to pay attention to authorship. Now, after obtaining my degree through the JDP, I am continuing research on the stroma of colorectal cancer as a postdoctoral researcher in the laboratory of Timothy Wang at Columbia University in the United States, through a connection of my supervisor in Adelaide. I feel that I can do research in my present environment precisely because of the personal network and research results built through the JDP. Also, as this is my second time studying abroad, the experience of studying abroad as a graduate student has been useful, and it seemed to make it easier to proceed smoothly in both research and daily life. I would like to thank the doctors and staff of the International Affairs Office of Nagoya University and the people at the University of Adelaide, who gave me this valuable opportunity to study abroad and supported me during my stay. I also thank those who supervised my research: Professor Emeritus 髙橋雅英, Professor 榎本篤 and Professor 浅井直也 (now at Fujita Health University) of the Department of Tumor Pathology, and Dr. Worthley and Associate Professor Woods of the University of Adelaide.
